# From UniLend to Maxi: The Next Chapter for Our Community

When we started UniLend, we set out with an ambitious goal: to make decentralised finance more open and permissionless.

A lot has happened since then.

The market has changed. The way people interact with crypto has changed. The products people use every day have changed. And, over time, our own understanding of where we could create the most value has changed as well. Today, we want to share an important update with the UniLend community.

After ceasing active development on UniLend Protocol last year, our team began working on what comes next. That work has led us to **Maxi**, a new decentralised social-first crypto trading platform designed to improve the way people discover, understand and trade assets across crypto.  
More importantly, we want the UniLend community to be part of this next chapter.

**All** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **holders will be offered a 1:1 migration from** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **to** [**$MAXI**](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click)**.**

This is not simply about moving from one token to another. It is our way of making sure that the community that supported us through the UniLend journey has an opportunity to participate in what we are building next.

## Looking back at UniLend

UniLend began at a very different point in the crypto market.

Our original thesis was that DeFi should not be limited to a small number of assets selected by centralized teams or governed by restrictive listing processes. We believed there was room for a more permissionless financial infrastructure where a much broader universe of tokens could participate.

That belief led us to build UniLend and, later, expand on that vision with new products and iterations. Like any startup journey, there were periods where things moved quickly and periods where we had to rethink assumptions.

We eventually launched the next iteration of UniLend Finance into a market that looked very different from the one in which we had started building. User behaviour had shifted, liquidity had moved, and the broader DeFi market had changed considerably.

We continued building and trying different approaches, but the product did not achieve the level of traction required to make the business sustainable. At the same time, our available runway came to an end.

Last year, we made the difficult decision to cease active development and operations around UniLend.

It was not a decision we made lightly. We had spent years building UniLend, working alongside our community and seeing [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) become a part of the portfolios and identities of people around the world. Walking away from active development without knowing exactly what would come next was difficult for everyone involved.

But continuing to spend resources on a product simply because we had spent years building it would not have been responsible either.

We needed to take what we had learned, look honestly at where crypto was moving, and decide what we believed was worth building for the next cycle rather than the previous one.

## What we learned

One of the biggest lessons from UniLend was that infrastructure alone is not enough.

Crypto users ultimately care about what they can do.

Over the last few years, trading has become one of the clearest and most persistent activities across the industry. At the same time, the trading experience itself has become increasingly fragmented.

A user’s portfolio may sit across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and several other ecosystems. Discovery happens on social platforms. Research happens across project websites, documentation, X, analytics tools and community conversations. Execution happens somewhere else entirely.

Users are expected to manage different wallets, different networks and different interfaces while constantly moving between tools.

We felt there had to be a better experience. That became the starting point for Maxi.

## Introducing Maxi

**Maxi is a decentralised social-first crypto trading platform built across major chains, including Bitcoin.**

The premise is straightforward: crypto trading is already social.

People discover new assets through other people. They follow traders, communities and narratives. They see what others are buying, selling and talking about before deciding whether something deserves their attention.

Most trading platforms, however, still treat the social and trading experiences as two separate worlds.

With Maxi, we are bringing them closer together.

Users will be able to discover assets and trading activity through a social-first experience, understand what is happening around a project, and move from discovery to action without navigating a fragmented collection of applications. We have also spent a significant amount of time simplifying the trading experience itself.

Crypto users should not have to think constantly about which wallet they need, where their funds are located, or how they are going to move assets between different ecosystems before they can make a trade.

Maxi is being built around the idea that much of this complexity should disappear into the product.

The result we are working toward is a trading experience that feels considerably simpler even though the infrastructure underneath it spans multiple chains.

## Helping traders understand more, faster

Discovery is only one part of trading.

Finding a new token on your timeline may take seconds. Understanding what the project actually does can take considerably longer. The usual process involves opening the project’s website, reading documentation, looking through announcements and searching through a mixture of facts and opinions before deciding whether the project is worth investigating further.

We believe technology can make that process more efficient.

One of the first AI-assisted features inside Maxi is designed to review information from a project’s official sources and produce a concise explanation of what the project is and what it does.

The purpose is not to replace research or tell someone what to buy.

It is to help a trader answer a much simpler question quickly:

### **Is this something I want to spend more time researching, or should I move on?**

In a market where hundreds of projects compete for attention, saving that time matters.

This research layer sits alongside Maxi’s social experience. Users can understand what a project says it is building while separately seeing what traders and the market are saying about it.

We think keeping those two perspectives together, without confusing one for the other, can make crypto discovery considerably more useful.

## Why Maxi is a new project

Maxi is not a new version of the UniLend lending protocol. It is a new product built around a different market opportunity.

The team, however, carries forward years of experience from building UniLend: shipping financial products on-chain, working across crypto ecosystems, operating through multiple market cycles and, importantly, learning from things that did not work as we expected.

There is a tendency in crypto to present every chapter as a straight line of success. That has not been our experience.

We built. We succeeded in some areas. We made mistakes in others. The market changed. Some assumptions proved wrong. Eventually, we reached a point where continuing UniLend in its existing direction was no longer sustainable. What matters to us now is what we do with those lessons.

Maxi is the result of that process.

## The UniLend community remains part of our journey

There was one question we felt strongly about while deciding how to move forward:

### **What happens to the people who supported UniLend and continued holding** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **?**

It would have been easier to treat Maxi as something entirely separate.

We don’t believe that would be right.

UniLend would never have existed without its community. For years, people supported the project, participated in the ecosystem, held [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click), provided feedback, created content, helped other users and stayed with us through different versions of the protocol.

We value that history.

And we do not want to start our next journey by leaving that community behind.

For that reason, we intend to provide every [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) holders with the opportunity to migrate their tokens into [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click).

## [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration

The migration ratio will be:  
**1** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)**→ 1** [**$MAXI**](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click)

In other words, an eligible holder migrating 1,000 [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) would receive 1,000 [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) under the migration program.

The 1:1 ratio refers to the **number of tokens being migrated**. It should not be interpreted as a representation or guarantee of market price, monetary value or future value between [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) and [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click).

A dedicated allocation of [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) will be made available for the migration of eligible [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click).

We will publish a separate, detailed migration announcement containing all of the information holders need before the process begins,

**There is no migration action required from** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **holders today.**

Please do not connect your wallet to any website claiming to offer the [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration until an official migration link has been published through UniLend’s verified communication channels.

We expect attempts to impersonate the team once migration information becomes public. The UniLend or Maxi team will never ask you to send us your private key, seed phrase or wallet credentials.

Further details will be communicated before the migration begins.

## Why we chose a 1:1 migration

We wanted the transition to be simple to understand.

Rather than designing a complicated conversion formula, we want eligible UniLend token holders to have a clear route into the new ecosystem.

If you supported UniLend and continue to hold [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click), this migration provides an opportunity to become part of Maxi from the beginning. We also believe it better reflects how we see the relationship between the two communities.

Maxi is a new product, but the team is not starting from zero.

The experience, relationships, lessons and community that came from UniLend are all part of how we arrived here.

The migration is our way of acknowledging that.

### What happens to UniLend?

Active development and operations around the UniLend product were ceased last year, and our development focus has since moved to Maxi.

Where required, we will provide additional information relating to existing UniLend infrastructure, products and community channels separately.

The [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration is intended to give token holders a path into the new ecosystem rather than leaving them disconnected from the work the team is doing next.

We will communicate clearly as the migration progresses so holders have sufficient information to make their own decision about whether they wish to participate.

## What comes next for Maxi

We have deliberately kept Maxi relatively quiet while building.

That is about to change.

The first version of Maxi brings together several ideas we believe are important for the next generation of crypto trading:

### **A social-first experience.**

Trading has always been influenced by people, communities and conversations. Maxi makes that behaviour a native part of the product rather than something that happens somewhere else.

### **Support across major crypto ecosystems.**

Crypto is no longer a single-chain market. Maxi is being designed for users whose activity spans multiple ecosystems, including Bitcoin.

### **A simpler trading experience.**

Users should be able to focus on the asset and the trade instead of constantly thinking about the infrastructure underneath it.

### **Faster project understanding.**

AI-assisted research will help users quickly understand unfamiliar projects using their official sources before deciding whether they want to investigate further.

These are only the first pieces.

Our ambition is to keep improving the experience around how people discover and trade assets across crypto while removing as much unnecessary complexity as we can.

## A word to the UniLend community

To everyone who has been part of UniLend over the years: Thank You.

Some of you have been with us since the earliest days. Some joined later. Some contributed directly, while many simply supported the project and believed in what we were trying to build. We know the last phase of UniLend was not the outcome any of us had hoped for.

We also know that trust is earned through actions rather than announcements. That is one of the reasons this migration matters to us.

We could not change how the market evolved, and we could not force a product to achieve traction simply because we wanted it to. But we can decide how we treat the people who supported us while we built it. We do not want to move forward by pretending UniLend never happened.

We want to move forward with the lessons it gave us and give the community that supported us an opportunity to come along. UniLend was an important chapter for our team. Maxi is the next one.

After ceasing active development on UniLend Protocol last year, our team began working on what comes next. That work has led us to **Maxi**, a new decentralised social-first crypto trading platform designed to improve the way people discover, understand and trade assets across crypto.  
More importantly, we want the UniLend community to be part of this next chapter.

**All** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **holders will be offered a 1:1 migration from** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **to** [**$MAXI**](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click)**.**

This is not simply about moving from one token to another. It is our way of making sure that the community that supported us through the UniLend journey has an opportunity to participate in what we are building next.

## Looking back at UniLend

UniLend began at a very different point in the crypto market.

Our original thesis was that DeFi should not be limited to a small number of assets selected by centralized teams or governed by restrictive listing processes. We believed there was room for a more permissionless financial infrastructure where a much broader universe of tokens could participate.

That belief led us to build UniLend and, later, expand on that vision with new products and iterations. Like any startup journey, there were periods where things moved quickly and periods where we had to rethink assumptions.

We eventually launched the next iteration of UniLend Finance into a market that looked very different from the one in which we had started building. User behaviour had shifted, liquidity had moved, and the broader DeFi market had changed considerably.

We continued building and trying different approaches, but the product did not achieve the level of traction required to make the business sustainable. At the same time, our available runway came to an end.

Last year, we made the difficult decision to cease active development and operations around UniLend.

It was not a decision we made lightly. We had spent years building UniLend, working alongside our community and seeing [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) become a part of the portfolios and identities of people around the world. Walking away from active development without knowing exactly what would come next was difficult for everyone involved.

But continuing to spend resources on a product simply because we had spent years building it would not have been responsible either.

We needed to take what we had learned, look honestly at where crypto was moving, and decide what we believed was worth building for the next cycle rather than the previous one.

## What we learned

One of the biggest lessons from UniLend was that infrastructure alone is not enough.

Crypto users ultimately care about what they can do.

Over the last few years, trading has become one of the clearest and most persistent activities across the industry. At the same time, the trading experience itself has become increasingly fragmented.

A user’s portfolio may sit across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and several other ecosystems. Discovery happens on social platforms. Research happens across project websites, documentation, X, analytics tools and community conversations. Execution happens somewhere else entirely.

Users are expected to manage different wallets, different networks and different interfaces while constantly moving between tools.

We felt there had to be a better experience. That became the starting point for Maxi.

## Introducing Maxi

**Maxi is a decentralised social-first crypto trading platform built across major chains, including Bitcoin.**

The premise is straightforward: crypto trading is already social.

People discover new assets through other people. They follow traders, communities and narratives. They see what others are buying, selling and talking about before deciding whether something deserves their attention.

Most trading platforms, however, still treat the social and trading experiences as two separate worlds.

With Maxi, we are bringing them closer together.

Users will be able to discover assets and trading activity through a social-first experience, understand what is happening around a project, and move from discovery to action without navigating a fragmented collection of applications. We have also spent a significant amount of time simplifying the trading experience itself.

Crypto users should not have to think constantly about which wallet they need, where their funds are located, or how they are going to move assets between different ecosystems before they can make a trade.

Maxi is being built around the idea that much of this complexity should disappear into the product.

The result we are working toward is a trading experience that feels considerably simpler even though the infrastructure underneath it spans multiple chains.

## Helping traders understand more, faster

Discovery is only one part of trading.

Finding a new token on your timeline may take seconds. Understanding what the project actually does can take considerably longer. The usual process involves opening the project’s website, reading documentation, looking through announcements and searching through a mixture of facts and opinions before deciding whether the project is worth investigating further.

We believe technology can make that process more efficient.

One of the first AI-assisted features inside Maxi is designed to review information from a project’s official sources and produce a concise explanation of what the project is and what it does.

The purpose is not to replace research or tell someone what to buy.

It is to help a trader answer a much simpler question quickly:

### **Is this something I want to spend more time researching, or should I move on?**

In a market where hundreds of projects compete for attention, saving that time matters.

This research layer sits alongside Maxi’s social experience. Users can understand what a project says it is building while separately seeing what traders and the market are saying about it.

We think keeping those two perspectives together, without confusing one for the other, can make crypto discovery considerably more useful.

## Why Maxi is a new project

Maxi is not a new version of the UniLend lending protocol. It is a new product built around a different market opportunity.

The team, however, carries forward years of experience from building UniLend: shipping financial products on-chain, working across crypto ecosystems, operating through multiple market cycles and, importantly, learning from things that did not work as we expected.

There is a tendency in crypto to present every chapter as a straight line of success. That has not been our experience.

We built. We succeeded in some areas. We made mistakes in others. The market changed. Some assumptions proved wrong. Eventually, we reached a point where continuing UniLend in its existing direction was no longer sustainable. What matters to us now is what we do with those lessons.

Maxi is the result of that process.

## The UniLend community remains part of our journey

There was one question we felt strongly about while deciding how to move forward:

### **What happens to the people who supported UniLend and continued holding** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **?**

It would have been easier to treat Maxi as something entirely separate.

We don’t believe that would be right.

UniLend would never have existed without its community. For years, people supported the project, participated in the ecosystem, held [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click), provided feedback, created content, helped other users and stayed with us through different versions of the protocol.

We value that history.

And we do not want to start our next journey by leaving that community behind.

For that reason, we intend to provide every [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) holders with the opportunity to migrate their tokens into [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click).

## [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration

The migration ratio will be:  
**1** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)**→ 1** [**$MAXI**](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click)

In other words, an eligible holder migrating 1,000 [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) would receive 1,000 [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) under the migration program.

The 1:1 ratio refers to the **number of tokens being migrated**. It should not be interpreted as a representation or guarantee of market price, monetary value or future value between [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) and [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click).

A dedicated allocation of [$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) will be made available for the migration of eligible [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click).

We will publish a separate, detailed migration announcement containing all of the information holders need before the process begins,

**There is no migration action required from** [**$UFT**](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click) **holders today.**

Please do not connect your wallet to any website claiming to offer the [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration until an official migration link has been published through UniLend’s verified communication channels.

We expect attempts to impersonate the team once migration information becomes public. The UniLend or Maxi team will never ask you to send us your private key, seed phrase or wallet credentials.

Further details will be communicated before the migration begins.

## Why we chose a 1:1 migration

We wanted the transition to be simple to understand.

Rather than designing a complicated conversion formula, we want eligible UniLend token holders to have a clear route into the new ecosystem.

If you supported UniLend and continue to hold [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click), this migration provides an opportunity to become part of Maxi from the beginning. We also believe it better reflects how we see the relationship between the two communities.

Maxi is a new product, but the team is not starting from zero.

The experience, relationships, lessons and community that came from UniLend are all part of how we arrived here.

The migration is our way of acknowledging that.

### What happens to UniLend?

Active development and operations around the UniLend product were ceased last year, and our development focus has since moved to Maxi.

Where required, we will provide additional information relating to existing UniLend infrastructure, products and community channels separately.

The [$UFT](https://x.com/search?q=%24UFT&src=cashtag_click)→[$MAXI](https://x.com/search?q=%24MAXI&src=cashtag_click) migration is intended to give token holders a path into the new ecosystem rather than leaving them disconnected from the work the team is doing next.

We will communicate clearly as the migration progresses so holders have sufficient information to make their own decision about whether they wish to participate.

## What comes next for Maxi

We have deliberately kept Maxi relatively quiet while building.

That is about to change.

The first version of Maxi brings together several ideas we believe are important for the next generation of crypto trading:

### **A social-first experience.**

Trading has always been influenced by people, communities and conversations. Maxi makes that behaviour a native part of the product rather than something that happens somewhere else.

### **Support across major crypto ecosystems.**

Crypto is no longer a single-chain market. Maxi is being designed for users whose activity spans multiple ecosystems, including Bitcoin.

### **A simpler trading experience.**

Users should be able to focus on the asset and the trade instead of constantly thinking about the infrastructure underneath it.

### **Faster project understanding.**

AI-assisted research will help users quickly understand unfamiliar projects using their official sources before deciding whether they want to investigate further.

These are only the first pieces.

Our ambition is to keep improving the experience around how people discover and trade assets across crypto while removing as much unnecessary complexity as we can.

## A word to the UniLend community

To everyone who has been part of UniLend over the years: Thank You.

Some of you have been with us since the earliest days. Some joined later. Some contributed directly, while many simply supported the project and believed in what we were trying to build. We know the last phase of UniLend was not the outcome any of us had hoped for.

We also know that trust is earned through actions rather than announcements. That is one of the reasons this migration matters to us.

We could not change how the market evolved, and we could not force a product to achieve traction simply because we wanted it to. But we can decide how we treat the people who supported us while we built it. We do not want to move forward by pretending UniLend never happened.

We want to move forward with the lessons it gave us and give the community that supported us an opportunity to come along. UniLend was an important chapter for our team. Maxi is the next one.

Permissionless DeFi Protocol

Unilend welcomes every asset to the defi ecosystem by opening up lending and borrowing functionalities to every ERC20 token through permissionless listing.

Create an Isolated Dual Asset Pool to enable Permissionless Lending and Borrowing for any asset pair without any risk to other assets.

Lenders enjoy the flexibility to choose the assets against which they wish to lend by selecting a corresponding pool.

Token holders can manage LVR for pools, price oracle sources and other changes through on-chain governance

User friendly interface to build, tokenize and launch AI agents without the need for coding.

Smart Mempools with Intents

Unilend introduces Numa Network that address the gas fees complexities, rigidity in transaction scheduling, and the complexities of cross-chain intents.

Unprecedented control and flexibility in transaction execution using intent driven programmable mempools.

Simplified user experience across all blockchains by eliminating the need for managing gas fees across multiple addresses.

Build Intent-driven dApps where transactions are automatically triggered based on predefined rules and conditions.

<h3 class="graf graf--h3 graf-after--h3" id="87fb">Overview:</h3>
<p class="graf graf--p graf-after--h3" id="2879">On January 13, 2025, the UniLend V2 (<a class="markup--anchor markup--p-anchor" data-href="https://x.com/UniLend_Finance" href="https://x.com/UniLend_Finance" rel="noopener" target="_blank">@UniLend_Finance</a>) contract on Ethereum was exploited due to incorrect health factor validation in the <code class="markup--code markup--p-code">redeemUnderlying</code> function. The flaw allowed an attacker to manipulate share prices and inflate collateral value, leading to improper health factor calculations. This enabled the attacker to withdraw collateral without adequate checks, resulting in a loss of approximately <strong class="markup--strong markup--p-strong">61 stETH (~$200k)</strong>.</p>
<h3 class="graf graf--h3 graf-after--p" id="9b0e">Smart Contract Hack Overview:</h3>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--h3" id="4a62"><strong class="markup--strong markup--li-strong">Attack Transaction: </strong><a class="markup--anchor markup--li-anchor" data-href="https://etherscan.io/tx/0x44037ffc0993327176975e08789b71c1058318f48ddeff25890a577d6555b6ba" href="https://etherscan.io/tx/0x44037ffc0993327176975e08789b71c1058318f48ddeff25890a577d6555b6ba" rel="noopener" target="_blank">0x44037</a></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="c644"><strong class="markup--strong markup--li-strong">Attacker’s Address: </strong><a class="markup--anchor markup--li-anchor" data-href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x55f5f8058816d5376df310770ca3a2e294089c33" href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x55f5f8058816d5376df310770ca3a2e294089c33" rel="noopener" target="_blank">0x55F5f</a>, <a class="markup--anchor markup--li-anchor" data-href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x6a1f503bfec09b6a5d3efdddea8ba9dceb9ec2d1" href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x6a1f503bfec09b6a5d3efdddea8ba9dceb9ec2d1" rel="noopener" target="_blank">0x6a1F5</a></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="4095"><strong class="markup--strong markup--li-strong">UniLendV2Core Contract:</strong> <a class="markup--anchor markup--li-anchor" data-href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x7f2e24d2394f2bdabb464b888cb02eba6d15b958" href="https://etherscan.io/address/0x7f2e24d2394f2bdabb464b888cb02eba6d15b958" rel="noopener" target="_blank">0x7f2E2</a></li>
</ul>
<figure class="graf graf--figure graf-after--li" id="5094"><img decoding="async" onerror="this.src='https://blog.solidityscan.com/wp-content/plugins/replace-broken-images/images/default.jpg'" class="graf-image" data-height="1010" data-image-id="1*SLvPP1RnMDnBgsE0UuGCjw.png" data-is-featured="true" data-width="1375" src="/wp-content/uploads/medium/1_SLvPP1RnMDnBgsE0UuGCjw.png" /><figcaption class="imageCaption">Fig: Attack transaction</figcaption></figure>
<h3 class="graf graf--h3 graf-after--figure" id="962b">Decoding the Smart Contract Vulnerability:</h3>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--h3" id="e1d0">The root cause of the exploit was the improper health factor validation in the <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">redeemUnderlying</code> function, combined with vulnerabilities in the <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">userBalanceOftoken1</code> function, and incorrect operation sequencing.</li>
</ul>
<figure class="graf graf--figure graf-after--li" id="5baa"><img decoding="async" onerror="this.src='https://blog.solidityscan.com/wp-content/plugins/replace-broken-images/images/default.jpg'" class="graf-image" data-height="908" data-image-id="1*yPSxiZbMQk2nqlEBmKW1IQ.png" data-width="1723" src="/wp-content/uploads/medium/1_yPSxiZbMQk2nqlEBmKW1IQ.png" /><figcaption class="imageCaption">Fig: reedemUnderlying() Function</figcaption></figure>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--figure" id="0abd">In the <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">redeemUnderlying</code> function:</li>
</ul>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--li" id="165c"><p>LP tokens are burned.</p></blockquote>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--blockquote" id="485d"><p>The health factor is checked using the <code class="markup--code markup--blockquote-code">userBalanceOftoken1</code> function.</p></blockquote>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--blockquote" id="db34"><p>Collateral is transferred to the user. However, the health factor calculation is performed using outdated pool balances (<code class="markup--code markup--blockquote-code">token0.balanceOf(address(this))</code> or <code class="markup--code markup--blockquote-code">token1.balanceOf(address(this))</code>), as the token balances are not updated immediately after burning LP tokens.</p></blockquote>
<figure class="graf graf--figure graf-after--blockquote" id="ef49"><img decoding="async" onerror="this.src='https://blog.solidityscan.com/wp-content/plugins/replace-broken-images/images/default.jpg'" class="graf-image" data-height="438" data-image-id="1*n0wU3aVjtn1a0JSpab21bQ.png" data-width="1198" src="/wp-content/uploads/medium/1_n0wU3aVjtn1a0JSpab21bQ.png" /><figcaption class="imageCaption">Fig: Vulnerable userBalanceOftoken1() Function</figcaption></figure>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--figure" id="44f2">The<code class="markup--code markup--li-code">userBalanceOftoken1</code> function calculates <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">lendBalance</code> using the following logic:<br /><code class="markup--code markup--li-code">_lendBalance1 = getShareValue(_totTokenBalance1, _tm1.totalLendShare, _positionMt.token1lendShare);</code></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="c0af">Here, <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">_totTokenBalance1</code> is derived from: <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">tokenBalance1.add(_tm1.totalBorrow);</code></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="5d6a">Since <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">tokenBalance1</code> reflects the current contract balance and does not account for tokens already allocated or pending withdrawal, the computation inflates the apparent <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">lendBalance</code>.</li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="3461">This issue is aggravated when the pool has significant liquidity, allowing a small lending share to correspond to a disproportionately high <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">lendBalance</code>.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--li" id="9a64"><p>So, the sequence of operations in the <code class="markup--code markup--blockquote-code">redeemUnderlying</code> function is flawed like this:<br />1. LP tokens are burned.<br />2. The health factor is checked using outdated pool balances.<br />3. Collateral is transferred to the user.</p></blockquote>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--blockquote" id="f4d2"><p>This order of operations enabled the attacker to exploit the inflated <code class="markup--code markup--blockquote-code">lendBalance</code> calculated before the pool balances are updated.</p></blockquote>
<blockquote class="graf graf--blockquote graf-after--blockquote" id="31ee"><p>Instead, a correct sequence would be to update the token balances (via token transfer) <em class="markup--em markup--blockquote-em">before</em> performing the health factor check.</p></blockquote>
<figure class="graf graf--figure graf-after--blockquote" id="ad2d"><img decoding="async" onerror="this.src='https://blog.solidityscan.com/wp-content/plugins/replace-broken-images/images/default.jpg'" class="graf-image" data-height="69" data-image-id="1*FT3Gh9JUnj4SeYw7yQy-mw.png" data-width="978" src="/wp-content/uploads/medium/1_FT3Gh9JUnj4SeYw7yQy-mw.png" /></figure>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--figure" id="a0c2">Also, the <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">getShareByValue</code> function performs the following calculation:<code class="markup--code markup--li-code">return (_valueAmount.mul(_totalSupply)).div(_totalAmount);<br /></code>This division is prone to rounding errors in favor of the user. A more precise approach would be to use a rounding-up division method (<code class="markup--code markup--li-code">divUp</code>) to ensure the protocol is not over-allocating tokens.</li>
</ul>
<p class="graf graf--p graf-after--li" id="b65b"><strong class="markup--strong markup--p-strong">Attack Flow:</strong></p>
<figure class="graf graf--figure graf-after--p" id="add5"><img decoding="async" onerror="this.src='https://blog.solidityscan.com/wp-content/plugins/replace-broken-images/images/default.jpg'" class="graf-image" data-height="301" data-image-id="1*QaZ2_Nu8UlSokjpcAbJa5w.png" data-width="2219" src="/wp-content/uploads/medium/1_QaZ2_Nu8UlSokjpcAbJa5w.png" /><figcaption class="imageCaption">Fig: Attack Calls Flow</figcaption></figure>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--figure" id="d5cf"><em class="markup--em markup--li-em">The attacker deposited a massive amount of USDC (60M) into the lending pool, obtaining a small number of lending shares due to the large liquidity in the pool.</em></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="2867"><em class="markup--em markup--li-em">They borrowed stETH and initiated withdrawals using the </em><code class="markup--code markup--li-code"><em class="markup--em markup--li-em">redeemUnderlying</em></code><em class="markup--em markup--li-em"> function.</em></li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="1af6">By exploiting the flawed health factor validation, they managed to withdraw all their USDC while keeping the stETH collateral, resulting in <strong class="markup--strong markup--li-strong">a net gain of approximately 61 stETH (~$200K).</strong></li>
</ul>
<h3 class="graf graf--h3 graf-after--li" id="be38">Mitigation and Best Practices:</h3>
<ul class="postList">
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--h3" id="d618">Ensure that the health factor is validated <em class="markup--em markup--li-em">after</em> updating the pool’s token balances (via token transfers) and <em class="markup--em markup--li-em">before</em> burning LP tokens or transferring collateral. This prevents the use of outdated balances during health factor calculations, effectively eliminating this exploit vector.</li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="804b">Adjust the logic to account for in-flight or pending token withdrawals when calculating <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">tokenBalance1</code> and <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">tokenBalance0</code>. Consider tracking allocated or reserved tokens separately to ensure accurate computations of <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">lendBalance</code> and <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">borrowBalance</code>.</li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="0401">Always ensure that the contract state (e.g., balances, shares, or pool totals) is updated before performing critical operations such as health factor validations or collateral calculations. This prevents the use of outdated or inconsistent state data.</li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="52ea">Maintain separate variables or mappings for tracking allocated, reserved, or in-flight token amounts. Avoid relying solely on the contract’s <code class="markup--code markup--li-code">balanceOf</code> function to determine the available liquidity or user balances.</li>
<li class="graf graf--li graf-after--li" id="3656">To prevent such vulnerabilities, the best Smart Contract auditors must examine the Smart Contracts for logical issues. </ul>

finance protocol UniLend Finance has reportedly been exploited on Ethereum, leading to a loss of roughly $197,000 worth of assets. On Jan. 12, real-time web3 security startup TenArmorAlert reported that an attacker exploited UniLend’s “redeem process” by manipulating a flaw in the share price calculation. This allowed the attacker to artificially inflate their collateral value and drain funds from the pool. The attacker deposited USDC and Lido Staked Ether (stETH) as collateral, borrowed the entire pool’s stETH, and then redeemed their initial deposits without repaying the borrowed tokens, effectively depleting the pool.At around 11:19:59 AM UTC, the exploit transaction was executed, with losses initially estimated by TenArmorAlert at $196.2K. However, a subsequent update from web3 security firm SlowMist placed the total losses slightly higher at $197.6K. As of publication, UniLend Finance had not addressed the exploit and request for additional insights from crypto.news remained unanswered. The DeFi sector has remained a prime target for bad actors in recent years. According to blockchain forensic firm PeckShield, approximately 60% of all exploits and scams in 2024 targeted this sector. One of the biggest exploits in 2024 was that of Radiant Capital, allegedly executed by the notorious Lazarus Group, resulting in a $50 million loss. The attackers impersonated a trusted former contractor of the DeFi protocol to deploy malware across the devices of at least three of the project’s developers. In November 2024, Thala protocol’s liquidity pools were drained for approximately $25.5 million, with the attacker leveraging a vulnerability in the protocol’s farming contracts. Fortunately, the attacker agreed to a $300,000 bounty and returned all stolen assets.","isAccessibleForFree":true}]}</script>

<p class="is-style-lead">Decentralized finance protocol UniLend Finance has reportedly been exploited on Ethereum, leading to a loss of roughly $197,000 worth of assets.</p>



<p>On Jan. 12, real-time web3 security startup TenArmorAlert <a href="https://x.com/TenArmorAlert/status/1878485163824337226" target="_blank" >reported</a> that an attacker exploited UniLend’s “redeem process” by manipulating a flaw in the share price calculation. This allowed the attacker to artificially inflate their collateral value and drain funds from the pool.</p>



<p>The attacker deposited <a href="https://crypto.news/price/usd-coin/">USDC</a> and Lido Staked Ether (<a href="https://crypto.news/price/lido-staked-ether/">stETH</a>) as collateral, borrowed the entire pool’s stETH, and then redeemed their initial deposits without repaying the borrowed tokens, effectively depleting the pool.<br><br>At around 11:19:59 AM UTC, the exploit transaction was executed, with losses initially estimated by TenArmorAlert at $196.2K. However, a subsequent <a href="https://x.com/SlowMist_Team/status/1878651772375572573" target="_blank" >update</a> from web3 security firm SlowMist placed the total losses slightly higher at $197.6K.</p>



<p>As of publication, UniLend Finance had not addressed the exploit and request for additional insights from crypto.news remained unanswered.</p>

<p>The DeFi sector has remained a prime target for bad actors in recent years. According to blockchain forensic firm PeckShield, approximately 60% of all exploits and scams in 2024 <a href="https://crypto.news/crypto-scams-and-hacks-surpass-3b-in-2024-up-15-from-2023/" target="_blank" >targeted</a> this sector.</p>



<p>One of the biggest exploits in 2024 was that of Radiant Capital, allegedly executed by the notorious Lazarus Group, resulting in a $50 million loss. The attackers impersonated a trusted former contractor of the DeFi protocol to deploy malware across the devices of at least three of the project’s developers.</p>



<p>In November 2024, Thala protocol’s liquidity pools were <a href="https://crypto.news/thala-protocol-resumes-operations-after-25-5m-exploit/" target="_blank" >drained</a> for approximately $25.5 million, with the attacker leveraging a vulnerability in the protocol’s farming contracts. Fortunately, the attacker agreed to a $300,000 bounty and returned all stolen assets.</p>

# Introduction

![](https://1350602574-files.gitbook.io/~/files/v0/b/gitbook-x-prod.appspot.com/o/spaces%2FQb4zsR9XKwVtMUKtPBk0%2Fuploads%2FIKSprk8pgy5DBbwYYbHw%2FUnilend%20Horizontal%20Logo%20\(1\).png?alt=media\&token=1b387e46-5364-4acf-814a-84a4803081e0)

UniLend Protocol is a permissionless decentralized money market protocol with lending and borrowing service through smart contracts. UniLend enables users to utilize their cryptocurrencies by supplying collateral to the network that may be borrowed by pledging over-collateralized cryptocurrencies. This creates a secure lending environment where the lender receives a compounded interest rate annually (APY) paid per block while the borrower pays interest on the cryptocurrency borrowed.

This document highlights the latest version of our protocol, UniLend V2, which brings the dual asset pools for lending borrowing with price feed oracles and gas optimization.

UniLend v2 is implemented as an entirely new set of contracts, available here. The UniLend v2 core contracts are partly upgradeable with some parameters controlled by governance.

UniLend is leading this with the launch of **Omnis, a multi-contract DeFi protocol** that builds the infrastructure to allow lending and borrowing of any ERC20 asset in a permissionless nature and expanding the horizon of DeFi. Our dev team lead by CTO Suryansh Kumar have built the protocol over the last 1 year to help developer communities and utilise these contracts to build new opportunities on the UniLend layer. And with this guide the UniLend team intends to highlight the most crucial aspect of our contracts and how various functions come into play. ### Create Pool UniLend protocol has concept of isolated pools of two different assets *token0* and *token1*. The pool is created from the function *createPool* in Core Contract and requires addresses of both the assets. Internally the function uses IUniLendV2Pool interface to create a pool from Pool Contract with default parameter values of *defaultInterestRate, default\_LTV, default\_LB, default\_RF.* ### Lend / Redeem The lend function needs to be called with parameter \_pool (pool address), and \_amount (int) to start lending of the assets. The token0 / token1 is selected respectively for +ve and -ve integer value of \_amount. The logic here gets or creates a Non Fungible Position for user and pool association using interface *IUnilendV2Position* and stores the information of each token’s address, lend balance and borrow balance for the user. ### Borrow / Repay Similar to the lend function the *borrow* function utilises the Pool Contract to create or update the Non Fungible Position. The function here requires *\_collateral\_amount (uint)* and *\_recipient (address)* in addition to *\_pool* and *\_amount.* The logic ensures validation of necessary liquidity in the pool to ensure the successful transaction. ### Liquidate To keep the UniLend system active and stable the our protocols rely on a distributed network of liquidators independently to keep the overall protocol healthy. These independent liquidators can use *liquidate* or *liquidateMulti* functions to help the system by repaying loans on behalf of defaulters and earn liquidation bonus. ### FlashLoan The flashloan function allows smart contracts to access the liquidity of the pool within one transaction in an uncollateralized borrowing as long as the amount taken plus a fee is returned. To initiate the flashloan function pass the following parameters *\_receiver :* The address of the contract receiving the funds. The receiver should implement the IFlashLoanReceiver interface. \_pool: the address of the principal reserve pool \_amount: the amount requested for this flashloan ## Summary UniLend V2 Relies on a Dual Asset Lending Pool model to offer risk mitigation and flexible lending options. All loans are backed by collateral and represented by Non-Fungible Tokens, which accrue the interests. Various protocol parameters such as collateralization ratio and interest rate vary for different assets.
